title: Vidura's riddle
hookLine: as the Pandavas leave, Vidura warns Yudhishthira in words nobody else can follow, and in Varanavata the new house smells wrong
carry: dharma protects those who protect it
tomorrow: how do you escape a house built to burn?

lines: A FAREWELL AT THE CITY'S EDGE.
VIDURA SPEAKS IN A HIDDEN TONGUE.
cards: A farewell at the edge of the city. The Pandavas and their mother are setting out for Varanavata, and an unhappy crowd has followed them out.

Vidura, their uncle, walks beside Yudhishthira and says something strange, in a tongue the crowd doesn't understand, the text says, that only Yudhishthira can follow. To anyone listening, it sounds like a riddle.

teach.b: Vidura's riddle goes something like this. There's a weapon not made of steel that can still destroy a body; whoever knows it can't be killed by it.
A fire that burns a whole forest can't reach the creatures that live in holes underground. Someone who knows the roads, who can find the way by the stars, will survive. Fire, holes, roads, stars.
Yudhishthira answers simply: I have understood. Later, on the road, Kunti asks what all that was about, and he tells her: Vidura was warning us of fire. Then they arrive.
Purochana greets them warmly, and after some days moves them into the new house. Walking through it, Yudhishthira catches a smell: fat, and lac. He turns to Bhima.
This house, he says, is made to burn. Who sends a warning like that?

teach.h: VIDURA: DHARMA, BORN AS A MAN.
teach.b: Earlier in the poem, the Mahabharata tells us who Vidura really is: Dharma himself, the god of right order, born as a man because of a sage's curse. And Yudhishthira is Dharma's son.
So many teachers read this scene as dharma looking after its own: the young man who keeps to truth is warned, quietly, by the one who embodies it.
Hindus carry a short line for this, from the Manusmriti: dharmo rakshati rakshitah.

teach.h: DHARMA PROTECTS THOSE WHO PROTECT IT.
teach.b: Dharma protects those who protect it. It doesn't promise that nothing bad happens to good people; the Pandavas are about to lose a great deal.
It means that holding to what's right keeps your eyes open, and keeps you near people who'll tell you the truth, even in a riddle.

how: Vidura is honored in Hindu tradition as a figure of dharma and wise counsel; his long advice to Dhritarashtra in the Udyoga Parva is still read on its own as the Vidura Niti.

o: the sage who taught Yudhishthira to read the stars
the elder brother who led the family to Varanavata
the uncle whose riddle warned the brothers of fire

p: Dharma himself, born as a man

s: Vidura warned the Pandavas openly before the crowd
he spoke in a tongue only Yudhishthira could follow, like a riddle.
Yudhishthira noticed the danger by smell
walking through the house, he smelled fat and lac and told Bhima it was made to burn.
dharmo rakshati rakshitah means good people never suffer
it means dharma protects those who protect it; the Pandavas still lose a great deal, but they're warned in time.

games.q: you're Yudhishthira. your uncle has just warned you in riddles of fire and holes in the ground. the crowd is watching. what do you do?
o: ask him to say it plainly.
games.why: he answers: I have understood. he explains it to Kunti later, on the road, and goes on to Varanavata.

practice: Many Hindus take a hard choice to an elder, the way Yudhishthira listened to Vidura. Bring one choice you're facing to mind, and ask the old question: what is dharma here, the right thing, not the easy one?
If you pray, ask for the clarity to see it. Then notice the room you're in, its sounds and smells, the way Yudhishthira noticed his.

wordCard.voice: Vidura, the uncle whose riddle of fire, holes, roads and stars warned Yudhishthira the new house was built to burn.

orig.note: Sanskrit dharma: right order, duty, what holds things together; Vidura is Dharma born as a man.

carryVoice: Your line: dharma protects those who protect it. A riddle, understood in time. Tomorrow: how do you escape a house built to burn?

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Adi Parva, Jatugriha Parva (Vidura's warning in a hidden tongue; Yudhishthira's reply; arrival at Varanavata; Yudhishthira recognizes the house)
